name: Fesenjan (Persian Walnut & Pomegranate Chicken Stew)
why: Peak pomegranate and walnut season in northern Iran, and Yaldā night — the Persian winter solstice feast — is this dish's traditional moment. Rich, tangy, deep: toasty ground walnuts and pomegranate molasses make a sauce that tastes far better than the ingredient list suggests, with only ~45 min of hands-off simmering.
author: Henry
ingredients: 1-1.5 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 tbsp olive oil + 1 tbsp butter, divided
Orange zest — 3 large strips (about 1/2 in x 2 in, peeled with a veggie peeler)
1 1/2 tsp salt, plus more to taste
To serve: saffron-infused basmati rice; garnish with pomegranate seeds and chopped Italian parsley

steps: Toast the walnuts in a Dutch oven over medium-low heat, stirring every couple of minutes, until deeply golden and fragrant — about 10 minutes.
While the walnuts toast, dice the onions, chop the garlic, cut the chicken into 1-inch pieces and season with salt and pepper, and drain and rinse the chickpeas if using.
Let the walnuts cool on a plate, then pulse in a food processor until finely ground — a dry meal, not a paste.
Wipe out the Dutch oven, add a drizzle of oil, and sear the chicken in batches until golden on all sides. Set aside.
In the same pan, heat the remaining oil and the butter over medium heat. Add the onions and cook until soft, golden and fragrant, about 5-6 minutes, then add the garlic and cook 3-4 more minutes.
When the onion-garlic mix is deeply golden, add turmeric, cumin, cinnamon, nutmeg, black pepper and the orange zest; toast 1-2 minutes until the spices smell sharp and warm.
Pour in the chicken stock, scraping up all the browned bits. Stir in the pomegranate molasses, honey, and 1 1/2 tsp salt, then add the seared chicken and ground walnuts. Bring to a boil, stirring.
Cover and drop to a low heat. Simmer 45 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes so the ground walnuts don't catch on the bottom.
Uncover, add the chickpeas if using, and simmer 10-15 more minutes until the stew has thickened, darkened to a deep maroon-brown, and the oil begins to rise and shimmer on the surface.
Taste and adjust — it should balance sweet, tangy and earthy; add a splash of water if it's too thick, more molasses if it needs tang.
Spoon over saffron basmati rice, scatter with pomegranate seeds and chopped parsley.

pro_tips: Walnut quality is everything — use fresh, not bitter walnuts (freeze whole walnuts to keep them fresh; rancid ones turn the whole stew off). If your walnuts smell off, skip straight to pre-ground toasted walnuts.
Fesenjan tastes even better the next day as the walnuts and molasses keep melding — make it a day ahead for a gathering. Leftovers keep 4 days refrigerated or 3 months frozen.

No pomegranate molasses? Reduce 1 cup pomegranate juice + 1 tbsp maple + 1 tbsp lemon juice + a pinch of salt for 45 minutes until it thickens to about 1/4 cup. Or go fully chickpea — it's traditionally a vegan-adaptable dish.
